html:
Ahmad Shah Massoud was an Afghan military leader from the Panjshir Valley, known as the "Lion of Panjshir". He fought the Soviets in the 1980s and the Taliban in the 1990s.

After the Soviet invasion of 1979, he became the best known commander of the mujahideen, the Islamic resistance. His fighters held the Panjshir against repeated Soviet offensives. When the communist government fell in 1992 he became defence minister, but the mujahideen parties then fought each other for Kabul, above all his forces against those of Gulbuddin Hekmatyar, and the city was badly damaged.

The Taliban took Kabul in 1996. Massoud withdrew to the northeast and led the Northern Alliance, the last serious resistance to them. On 9 September 2001, two al-Qaeda men posing as journalists killed him with a bomb hidden in their camera, two days before the 11 September attacks. Afghanistan later named him a national hero.
sum: Ahmad Shah Massoud was an Afghan military leader from the Panjshir Valley, known as the "Lion of Panjshir". He fought the Soviets in the 1980s and the Taliban in the 1990s.
